newsitem.title: UK: CBI says happy for UK to keep EMU options open.
newsitem.headline: CBI says happy for UK to keep EMU options open.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Wednesday it supported the government's official policy of keeping the option open on membership of a single European currency.
"We support the opt-out, we would not want to see that given up," the CBI's chief economic adviser Kate Barker told a news conference.
"We are happy to see the options kept open at the moment."
The CBI is currently consulting its members to determine a position on European economic and monetary union.
A draft consultation paper will be debated by CBI committees over the coming months.
The CBI said the paper will set out the complex business issues for and against EMU and offers three options.
Contrary to newspaper reports on Wednesday, these options include one which rules out EMU entry for the foreseeable future, it said.
Barker, also one of Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's independent advisers, said "foreseeable future" should not necessarily mean joining at some point.
The other two options support EMU entry in principle but differ in terms of timing and preconditions.
